method.method_summary: The notes do not show a single final base-year dollar value; they support a mixed, U.S.-centric sizing that triangulates supply-side quotas/trade data with demand-side dispensing, pricing, and patient counts. The supply chain starts with DEA aggregate production quota (42.4k kg) and allotted quota (38.418k kg); applying the note that retail distribution is about 70% of allotted quota gives roughly 26.9k kg retail, with imports/exports checked separately (U.S. amphetamine imports of 11,042 kg in 2020, 13,920 kg in 2021, 8,685 kg in 2022, ~13,043 kg in 2023). Demand is cross-checked via amphetamine pills dispensed (100M–200M pills/month), prescriptions (2.0M–4.5M/month), lisdexamfetamine pills (10M–60M/month), real per-pill prices, and a patient base of 15.5M diagnosed U.S. adults with about one-third taking stimulant medication.

method.method_summary: The notes triangulate three approaches for 2026. Household expenditure uses 9.92 million households, a SAR 78.1 billion furnishings/household-equipment pool, and a 0.05 kitchen-cabinetry allocation to reach SAR 3.91 billion. Production/trade adds SAR 2.80 billion domestic manufacturing plus SAR 501.3 million wooden imports and SAR 124.4 million aluminium import proxy, subtracts SAR 3.9 million exports to get SAR 3.42 billion apparent consumption, then applies a 15% design/distribution/installation uplift to reach SAR 3.93 billion. Installation/pricing adds 396,700 replacement, 50,000 new residential, and 35,700 commercial/B2B kitchens to get 482,400 installations and a SAR 3.96 billion value; the final triangulated average is SAR 3.93 billion, or USD 1.05 billion.
